panels.description: Every response resolved to exactly one class. rpc_error is an HTTP 200 carrying a JSON-RPC error object, which the HTTP-only failure rate cannot see; rpc_null is a call that succeeded and returned nothing.

panels.title: JSON-RPC error rate by method
panels.description: Share of a method's calls that came back with a JSON-RPC error object. Reported per method rather than per status, because a rate inside one status bucket is only ever 0 or 1.

panels.title: JSON-RPC error codes
panels.description: The codes the node itself returned, kept as labels rather than folded into a generic error counter.

panels.title: Response size by method
panels.description: Payload size distribution per method. The missing axis when comparing eth_getLogs across clients: a faster client returning less data is not a faster client.

panels.title: Offered vs delivered
panels.description: What the generator scheduled against what it actually sent. A gap means the run never offered the requested load, and the latency panels above describe only the requests that went out.

panels.title: Achieved request rate
panels.description: Requests per second the generator actually offered. Compare against the configured rps: a shortfall means the endpoint, not the target rate, set the pace.

panels.title: Dispatch delay
panels.description: How far behind schedule requests went out. This is the coordinated-omission error: while it is above zero the reported latencies describe a slower offered rate than the one configured.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Concurrent requests, and the peak reached. At the configured vus ceiling the generator is the limiter.

options.content:
### About these metrics

Every series is prefixed `bench_` and written by the runner over Prometheus remote write. **Trend values are cumulative from the start of a run**, so a latency panel reads "p99 so far" rather than p99 within the window — the same semantics k6 had.

`metrics/METRICS.md` lists every series with its labels and meaning, and maps each old `k6_*` name to its replacement. The previous dashboard is kept as **k6 Prometheus (archived)**.

Filter with the `testid` variable, which carries the `test_name` from the benchmark config.
